figures.caption: Fig. 1 Schematic of a representative interface model.The cathode slab exposes two distinct terminations at the interface, deﬁned as region A (LiCoO2-terminated, P2m2) and region B (Li-terminated, C2m1).

Fig. 2 Calculated Li+ diﬀusivities along the z-axis for six solid electrolytes and their interfaces with LixCoO2 cathodes at x = 0.5 and x = 1.0. “Oriented bulk” denotes the Li+ diﬀusivity computed in the corresponding bulk phase along the crystallographic direction parallel to the z-axis in the interface model.The oriented bulk diﬀusivities of LLZO, LLTO, and LiCoO2 are experimental values,28–30 because molecular dynamics simulations could not reliably capture Li+ transport in these materials due to its very slow diﬀusion. Diﬀusivities for the bulk discharged (LiCoO2) and charged (Li0.5CoO2) cathodes are shown on the right panel on a separate y-axis scale for reference, as their values span a much wider range than the interfacial and SEs' diﬀusivities.
Fig. 3 Spatial distribution of Li+ along the z-axis across the modeled solid-electrolyte/Li0.5CoO2 interfaces. Shaded regions A and B denote the two distinct interfacial regions.

Fig. 4 (a and b) Elemental proﬁles along the z-axis and interface structures after 1 ns of MD simulation for the Li7P3S11/Li0.5CoO2 (a) and Li10GeP2S12/Li0.5CoO2 (b) interfaces. The proﬁles were computed by averaging MD trajectories over the last 100 ps of a 1 ns simulation. (c and d) Evolution of the radial distribution functions (RDFs) for S–S (c) and P–P (d) pairs at these interfaces. For comparison, RDFs of reference compounds within the Li–Ge–P–S–O chemical space are also shown, retrieved from the Materials Project for phases with energy above hull less than 20 meV per atom.

Fig. 5 Elemental proﬁles along the z-axis and the atomic conﬁgurations after 1 ns simulations of the (a) Li3YCl6/Li0.5CoO2, (b) Li3YCl6/LiCoO2, (c) Li3InCl6/Li0.5CoO2 and (d) Li3InCl6/LiCoO2 interface models.
Fig. 6 Elemental proﬁles along the c-axis and the atomic conﬁgurations after 1 ns simulations of the (a) LLZO/Li0.5CoO2, (b) LLTO/Li0.5CoO2 interface models.
